text:
hao: Quick thought — propose splitting the continuous batcher into three explicit pipeline stages: ingest -> coalesce -> dispatch. Make queue boundaries first-class so admission, backpressure, and eviction contracts are clear. Thoughts?
emma: +1 for explicit boundaries. makes reasoning about backpressure & metrics much easier.
chris: Concern: who owns KV cache entries during stage handoff? eviction semantics can leak if ownership isn't explicit.
tess: Also need to think about warmup: dispatch needs hints about seq-len distribution earlier, otherwise we get cold-model penalties.
hao: Sketch of a small runtime API idea: enqueue(req) -> lease_token. Stages pull token, operate, then call release(token) on dispatch or evict(token). Token carries size/priority metadata.
emma: Can you paste a proto sketch so infra can review?
hao: ```proto
message LeaseToken {
  string id = 1;
  uint32 token_weight = 2; // approximate token count
  uint32 priority = 3; // 0 (low) - 10 (high)
  uint64 expires_at = 4;
}
service Batcher {
  rpc Enqueue(Req) returns (LeaseToken);
  rpc Release(LeaseToken) returns (Ack);
}
```
chris: Lease needs TTL + preemptible flag. If inflight evictions occur, the preemptible ones can be torn down quickly. Also add an opt-in 'fastpath' bit for tiny requests.
tess: Telemetry requirements: per-stage counters: ingest_enqueued, coalesce_wait_ms_p50/p95, dispatch_latency_ms_p50/p95, evictions_total. We must tie those to current dashboards.
emma: For migration, default to passthrough mode: old queue becomes ingest; new stages are behind a feature flag. Gradual rollout per shard.
chris: Operator knobs: soft-isolation headroom percent, eviction_hysteresis_ms, fastpath_threshold_tokens. We should pick sensible defaults.
hao: Proposed defaults: headroom 20%, eviction_hysteresis 50ms, fastpath_threshold 8 tokens. We'll calibrate with canary traffic.
infra-bot: deploy-batcher-refactor-canary started by @emma — id batcher-canary-2026-03-22-07
tess: Ordering edge-case: if a request gets evicted and retried we could process out-of-order. Need idempotent handlers or sequenced dedupe at the dispatch layer.
hao: Agree. include monotonic request_id and let dispatch dedupe for ~2s window. cheap in-memory LRU.
emma: Small follow-up: map old metric names to new stage metrics so alerts don't break during rollout. We should add translation shim in Telemetry service.
chris: I'll draft an RFC follow-up with sequence diagrams and a migration checklist. Assigning to @chris and @hao. Timeline: proto by EOW, RFC by next Tue, feature-flagged rollout next sprint.
tess: :thumbsup: happy to help on telemetry mapping and dashboards.
hao: thanks — I'll push a prototype of the Enqueue/LeaseToken shim later today and open a PR for the proto.
emma: Please add a simple emulation harness so we can run load tests locally (coalesce timing + eviction scenarios).
chris: noted. I'll include a harness that can replay real traces and validate ordering + kv-cache hit behavior.
tess: tiny UX ask: include a human-readable "reason" in evict telemetry (e.g., "headroom", "hysteresis", "preempt") so SREs can triage quickly.
hao: will add reason string to evict event.
chris: RFC backlog item: decide whether lease tokens should be signed (to prevent clients forging priority). thoughts?
emma: Prefer signed tokens if external clients ever touch tokens. internal-only RPCs can skip for perf, but make signing pluggable.
hao: Good point. We'll make signing optional at transport layer.
ess: (typo) ignore
chris: I'll create the RFC PR and ping the runtime list when ready.
hao: cheers, thanks all for quick checks.
